title: Horizontal compatibility of fixed normalized tensor comparisons
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a scheme $W$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-pc-scheme]. Work on its small pro-etale site with independent object, arrow and coefficient universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $A$ for the completed integral coefficient sheaf and $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1})_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of actual coefficient sequence-site modules and finite coefficient modules, with exact evaluation $e_n$ [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site] and their closed tensor structures [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Fix reduction data $R$ [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data], with representative normalizations as specified in [lem-coef-normalized-reduction-models]. Assume evaluation tensor normalization $h_E$ and choose normalized finite quotient calculus $Q$. For arbitrary derived coefficient systems $P,V$ and $n\leq m$, let $F$ be derived extension from $B_m$ to $B_n$ and let $\alpha_X:F(e_mX)\longrightarrow e_nX$ be the adjunct under $Q.\mathrm{adjunction}$ of the actual horizontal transition of $X$. Then $F(R.\mathrm{evaluationTensor}(m)_{P,V})\,Q.\mathrm{tensor}_{e_mP,e_mV}\,(\alpha_P\otimes\alpha_V)=\alpha_{P\otimes V}\,R.\mathrm{evaluationTensor}(n)_{P,V}$, with all tensor comparison arrows pointing from the image of a tensor to the tensor of the images and composition read left to right. There is no normalized-input hypothesis and no internal-Hom assertion.

proof.text: Resolve both systems by flat-term K-flat complexes on the actual sequence site. Evaluation preserves flatness and K-flatness; use the ordinary evaluation tensor identification and its total-complex comparison.

On each local pure-tensor summand, horizontal transition of a tensor is the tensor of the two horizontal transitions. Under the ordinary quotient adjunction its adjunct is given by the unit 1 tensor x. Thus the two balanced tensor maps agree; summand generators and sheafification give equality on strict cochain systems. This is the tensor-reduction model calculation.

The normalization Q.ordinary_unit fixes the ordinary adjunct, Q.unit_model fixes its localization, and hE and Q.tensor_model identify both binary tensor comparisons on representatives. Cancel those comparisons and transport along K-flat replacement isomorphisms. The result is precisely the equality for the actual transition adjoints. Equal indices give the same formula; neither faithfulness of finite derived evaluation nor flatness of quotient rings is used.

theorem coefficientNormalizedTensorHorizontal
    (R : CoefficientDerivedSystemReduction l E W)
    (hE : CoefficientEvaluationTensorNormalization l E W R)
    (Q : CoefficientFiniteQuotientCalculus l E W R.toCoefficientDerivedSystemTensors)
    (P V : coefficientSequenceDerived l E W) {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) :
    (coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E W h).map
        ((R.evaluationTensor m).hom.app (P, V)) ≫
      (Q.tensor h).hom.app
        ((coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E W m).obj P,
          (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E W m).obj V) ≫
      (R.finiteClosed n).tensor.map
        (Prod.mkHom
          (coefficientSequenceTransitionAdjoint l E W R.toCoefficientDerivedSystemTensors Q h P)
          (coefficientSequenceTransitionAdjoint l E W R.toCoefficientDerivedSystemTensors Q h V)) =
    coefficientSequenceTransitionAdjoint l E W R.toCoefficientDerivedSystemTensors Q h
        (R.systemClosed.tensor.obj (P, V)) ≫
      (R.evaluationTensor n).hom.app (P, V)
